subject: SCCs execution options for Stellar Health — module selection + evidence request
messages:
From: Legal Team <legal@stellarhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: dpcompliance@healthboard.co.uk; Oliver Grant <oliver@mg-privacy.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SCCs and execution path for Stellar — need module guidance and evidence

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move toward contracting, our legal and privacy teams need clarity on the cross-border mechanism Redwood will rely on and a small set of evidentiary artifacts. A few specific asks: 

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood intends to execute the EU Standard Contractual Clauses as: (a) Controller -> Processor (Module 2) or (b) Processor -> Processor (Module 3) for Stellar Health? Our classification: Stellar is Controller; Redwood will be a Processor. We want to avoid re-routing that would require additional processor-to-processor SCCs unless unavoidable.

2) For UK transfers, do you use the UK Addendum or a separate UK SCCs execution flow?

3) Please provide the following evidence (redacted as needed): executed DPA/DPA template with SCCs marked, SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted), DPIA summary for healthcare workloads, and a short statement on key management (KMS/HSM) and pseudonymization measures.

4) Timeline: we need a signed mechanism in place before go-live (target: end of month). Can you confirm a timeline and whether you can send an execution-ready DocuSign package?

Attached is our SCCs questionnaire (Stellar_SCCs_questionnaire_v1.pdf) — we started filling it; feel free to annotate.

Best,
Amy Reynolds
Head of Legal Operations
Stellar Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Legal Team <legal@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SCCs and execution path for Stellar — need module guidance and evidence

Amy / team — thanks, and great to be moving this forward. Summary below and next steps.

Quick answer: Our standard, supported execution path for controller -> processor relationships is to sign the EU SCCs (Controller -> Processor) paired with the UK Addendum for UK-relevant transfers. That aligns with Stellar's Controller role and keeps the contract path straightforward (Option A).

Option A (preferred) — Recommended for Stellar
- EU SCCs: Controller -> Processor (Module 2)
- UK: UK Addendum attached to the DPA (we populate the UK-specific annex)
- Why: minimal re-characterization, clearer obligations for controller-driven instructions, and faster execution.

Option B (fallback) — Processor chaining scenario
- Processor -> Processor (Module 3) would be used only when Redwood is acting as a sub-processor passing data to another processor on behalf of Stellar and the legal flow requires processor-to-processor mapping. This is not our default for customer-hosted flows.

Evidence we can provide (attached/links)
- Redwood executed DPA template with SCCs placeholders (Stellar_DPA_marked-up.docx)
- SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted) and statement of any scope exclusions (redwood-soc2-summary-redacted.pdf)
- DPIA summary for healthcare workload patterns (redwood-dpia-summary.pdf)
- KMS statement: we use customer-specific KMS integrations for private deployments and HSM-backed keys in hosted mode.
- Processing activities annex: we'll draft the Processing Activities Annex for Stellar and include subprocessor list and subprocessors' jurisdictions.

Open items for us internally: Neha, Ben — can you confirm that the proposed Module 2 + UK Addendum language is acceptable from legal/contracting? Marcus — confirm we can provide the DPIA summary and whether any extra controls apply for the EU region private deployment.

Target: I'll prepare an execution-ready DocuSign packet (DPA + SCCs + UK Addendum) within 5 business days after we confirm Option A. If you want, I can send a clean and a marked version for review.

Action items
- Amy: confirm Option A works for Stellar (reply to this thread)
- Neha/Ben: review and flag any non-standard redlines
- Marcus: confirm DPIA controls and deployment notes by EOD Friday 2026-01-16

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Manager, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SCCs and execution path for Stellar — internal notes

Evelyn — quick internal note to support the external thread.

1) Legal position: I agree Option A (Controller -> Processor + UK Addendum) is the cleanest route. We'll prepare a Processing Activities Annex tailored to Stellar's PHI handling patterns and call out HIPAA adjacency. We should include explicit subprocessors and confirm they will accept SCCs.

2) Redlines to anticipate: customer teams often request (a) audit-rights language changes, (b) narrower data return/deletion timelines, and (c) stricter breach notice SLAs. I recommend pre-populating acceptable compromises in the DPA to speed negotiations.

3) DPIA / HIPAA: the DPIA summary will call out technical measures (pseudonymization in transit, tokenization at rest for identifiers, KMS compartmentalization). For hosted customers where PHI is in scope, we recommend the Dedicated/Private deployment offering and documenting that in the annex. Marcus — please confirm whether the EU private pool for Stellar can be reserved and whether there are any operational constraints (region, encryption-at-rest options).

4) Evidence package: send SOC2 summary, DPA template (marked), DPIA summary, and a standard evidence checklist we use for healthcare customers. We should avoid sending full SOC2 reports without an NDA; summary + bridge letter should suffice for now.

I'll prepare suggested DPA compromises and upload the marked DPA to the shared drive.

—Neha
Lead Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Evelyn — thanks for the clear note and Neha for the internal summary. We are comfortable proceeding with Option A (Controller -> Processor + UK Addendum). A few items before we sign:

- Please send the execution-ready DPA + SCCs + UK Addendum via DocuSign (we prefer one envelope).
- Attach the SOC2 summary (redacted) and DPIA summary you referenced; our privacy team will want to keep those.
- On subprocessors: please include the current subprocessor roster and confirm whether any subprocessors are outside EEA/UK/US.

If you can get the DocuSign out this week, we'll aim to sign on our side by Jan 27. Forwarding your previous messages for context.

Best,
Amy Reynolds
Head of Legal Operations
Stellar Health
